headline: Nussmeier Finds Hasty in Overtime as LSU Escapes Michigan 30-24
dek: The Tigers improve to 3-0 and climb to No. 2 in the power poll while the Wolverines fall to 1-2 and tumble to No. 12.
body: Overtime, 1:58 remaining, first and goal at the Michigan 4: Garrett Nussmeier drops back, scans the middle of the field and fires a dart to Woody Hasty for a four-yard touchdown that puts LSU ahead 30-24 and ultimately ends the game. Michigan had seen two field-goal attempts from Herbie Swanson miss — a 19-yarder wide and a 51-yarder short — and their overtime possession ended with those misses.

LSU struck first on a methodical 11-play, 80-yard opening drive capped by Tim Ferguson's one-yard plunge for a 7-0 lead. Michigan answered with Calvin Wendtland's three-yard score to tie it at 7, then LSU reclaimed the lead on Yousef Snow's 11-yard run. Eric Brock's four-yard touchdown knotted the score at 14 before Lilian Munoz's 29-yard field goal made it 17-14 at halftime. The Tigers pushed the margin to 10 on Mason Taylor's 29-yard catch in the third quarter, but Michigan rallied with Vance Boyer's one-yard reception and Swanson's 48-yard field goal to force overtime at 24-24.

The box score tells a story of two evenly matched offenses: Michigan outgained LSU 456-442 and held a 212-178 edge on the ground behind Wendtland's 99 yards, while Nussmeier threw for 275 yards and two scores to pace a 264-yard aerial attack. Third-down efficiency was nearly identical at 43% for LSU and 41% for Michigan, and each team recorded one interception in the play-by-play — Jakailin Johnson picking off Chip Gabriel in the second quarter and William Jackson intercepting Nussmeier in the third. Penalties were minimal at one apiece, and time of possession was virtually even. Nussmeier's 22-of-38, 275-yard, two-touchdown line lifts his season totals to 691 yards, seven touchdowns and a 101.1 rating, ninth in the PCFL in passing yards. Wendtland's 99 yards on nine carries pushes his season total to 189 yards at 9.4 per carry, second in the league.

The win moves LSU to 3-0 and vaults the Tigers from No. 4 to No. 2 in the power poll, keeping them in the hunt atop the Eastern Southern behind division leader Tennessee. Michigan drops to 1-2 and slides from No. 6 to No. 12, now chasing Notre Dame in the Western Central with a loss already on the ledger. Next week the Tigers host Penn State (1-2) while the Wolverines travel to face winless Michigan State.
turningPoint: Overtime, 1:58 — Nussmeier's four-yard touchdown pass to Hasty on first and goal gave LSU a 30-24 lead that held after Michigan's two missed field goals.
byTheNumbers: Michigan outgained LSU 456-442 but converted only 7 of 17 third downs (41%) and went 0-for-1 on fourth down, including a failed 4th-and-3 at the LSU 27 in the third quarter.
Nussmeier's 275 passing yards and two touchdowns raised his season total to 691 yards and seven scores, placing him ninth in the PCFL in passing yards.
Wendtland's 99 rushing yards on nine carries (11.0 avg.) pushed his season average to 9.4 yards per carry, second in the league behind only Jerrick Gibson.
Swanson missed two overtime field goals (19 yards wide, 51 yards short), leaving six points on the board in a six-point game.

unsungHero.name: Jakailin Johnson
unsungHero.why: His second-quarter interception of Gabriel gave LSU possession and preceded the field goal that made it 17-14 at halftime.
